fault: modular_robot_benchmarks/mission_trial.py:571-577 evaluates the trial's wall backstop after executor.spin_once(timeout_sec=0.1) in the same loop body, so the backstop only fires if spin_once returns. It does not always return. Replicate r9 of the round trip sat inside a single spin_once call for 6 h 15 m while the break condition on the line below it was continuously true. A campaign in this state stalls forever: no terminal record is written, no infrastructure_attempts.jsonl entry is appended, and mission_batch never reaches the next trial.
fix_owed: The backstop has to be reachable without spin_once cooperating. It must also not score a wedged observer as a robot outcome: mission_batch already retries terminal_status infrastructure_failure when the launch process is still alive (retryable_infrastructure_failure), which is the correct disposition for this. Any fix needs a regression test that wedges the spin and asserts the trial aborts.
interpretation: The runner was spinning, not deadlocked on a lock it would never get: it consumed 8.1% of a core throughout. Gazebo, the parameter bridge and the Nav2 nodes all stayed healthy and advanced simulated time to 20099.642 s while the mission observer's own clock stayed frozen at 163.512 s, so the observer lost /clock while everything else kept it. That is the same family as the discovery failures already on record here. What makes it cost a campaign rather than a trial is the watchdog placement, which is the defect this record is about.
not_yet_root_caused: Why the observer stopped receiving /clock at simulated 163.5 s, with FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS=SHM set and /dev/shm/fastrtps_* cleared before the campaign, is not established. r9's mission had reached its goal and passed both post-transition motion qualifications moments earlier, so the observer wedged at or just after mission completion.
observed: 2026-09-27/28, during the third 20-run round-trip re-collection attempt

raw_evidence.note: results/ is gitignored and the retention mechanism is the open ADR 0005 decision, so these paths are in the WSL clone at /home/checker/morphology_ws and are not archived. The digests identify them while they last.

status: DIAGNOSED, NOT FIXED. The fix is owed and no code change has been made.
teardown: The wedged runner, the simulator, the bridge and four surviving Nav2 nodes were killed and confirmed gone; /dev/shm/fastrtps_* was cleared and the container is stopped. The nine records are intact on disk.
why_it_is_not_a_simulated_clock_bug: The 0.1 s timeout timer spin_once builds is created on the executor's own clock, which rclpy sets to ClockType.STEADY_TIME (rclpy/executors.py:210), not on the node's sim clock. The wedge is inside spin_once itself, in the while True retry loop of Executor.wait_for_ready_callbacks (rclpy/executors.py:877 and 704/749), sampled twice with yielded_work True and timeout_nsec 100000000.
